item.title: America and China are fighting for the future of AI — chips are the battlefield
item.description: President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Washington as Huawei races to build a rival AI chip ecosystem that could displace American semiconductor dominance.
item.content:encoded:
When President Donald Trump sits down with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, the agenda will be crowded.

Trade. Tariffs. Rare earth minerals. National security. Supply chains.

But looming over all of it is a technological competition that could shape the balance of economic and military power for decades: artificial intelligence. And increasingly, the battle isn't simply about who builds the best AI model.

TRUMP-XI’S CHINA SUMMIT IS A DEFINING TEST FOR AMERICA IN THE NEW COLD WAR

It is about who controls the chips, computing infrastructure and technology ecosystem underneath it.

America remains the global leader in advanced AI technology and semiconductor design. But China is pushing aggressively to reduce its dependence on American technology, and Huawei has emerged as one of the most important companies in that effort. That should have Washington's full attention.

For years, the United States has used export controls to restrict China's access to advanced semiconductors and semiconductor-manufacturing technology, particularly technologies with potential military applications.

Those restrictions had a clear national-security objective: prevent America's most sophisticated technology from strengthening a strategic competitor's military capabilities. But there has also been an unintended consequence worth confronting. China accelerated its effort to build an AI ecosystem that doesn't need America.

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

Huawei expanded its Ascend AI-chip roadmap. Chinese developers adapted software and models to domestic hardware. Chinese companies poured resources into computing systems capable of compensating for some of the performance limitations of individual Chinese chips. And Huawei isn't standing still.

The company recently said demand for its AI computing equipment in China is exceeding supply. It is accelerating future generations of its Ascend processors and developing enormous computing systems capable of connecting vast numbers of chips.

That means the strategic question facing Washington has changed.

AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL

The question isn't simply: How do we keep sensitive American technology away from China? It is also: How do we make sure the rest of the world continues choosing American technology instead of China's? Those are related questions, but they aren't identical.

If American technology becomes inaccessible across too much of the global market, China has an enormous incentive to develop substitutes. Huawei has an enormous incentive to sell them. And governments and companies around the world have an enormous incentive to build around whatever technology they can reliably obtain.

THE AI REVOLUTION COULD BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY DISASTER IF WE AREN'T CAREFUL

Once developers write software for an ecosystem, companies construct computing infrastructure around it and countries invest billions deploying it, switching becomes much harder. That's why this isn't merely a chip-sales competition. It is an ecosystem competition.

America wants a world running on American chips, American software, American standards and American innovation. China wants to build an alternative. It wants a world in which Huawei and other Chinese companies provide a technology stack that Beijing controls and America cannot easily influence.

President Trump has taken a different approach from the Biden administration. His administration rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule while maintaining controls targeting technologies with serious national-security implications.

The administration has also allowed certain advanced chips to be considered for sale to approved Chinese customers under licensing requirements and security conditions. The theory is straightforward: protect the technologies most critical to national security without unnecessarily surrendering commercial markets to Chinese competitors. That distinction matters.

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

Nobody serious is arguing that America should simply hand China unrestricted access to technology that could materially enhance advanced weapons, military AI, surveillance or other sensitive capabilities.

National security comes first. But there is a difference between protecting America's crown-jewel technology and adopting restrictions so sweeping that they accelerate China's determination to replace American technology throughout the commercial market. Because Huawei's goal isn't merely to survive American restrictions.

Huawei wants to compete. It wants Chinese chips powering Chinese AI. It wants Chinese computing infrastructure supporting Chinese models. And ultimately, Chinese technology companies want customers outside China using their systems.

That's why the next phase of this competition will be fought over which chips countries buy, which computing systems they install, which software developers learn and which technology stack becomes the default infrastructure for the AI economy.

America has enormous advantages. We have extraordinary semiconductor designers, the world's leading AI companies, deep capital markets, world-class universities, entrepreneurs and an innovation culture China has spent decades trying to replicate.

But technological leadership isn't permanent. It has to be defended. And sometimes the greatest threat to American leadership isn't that China suddenly invents something better. It's that America creates policies that make its own technology harder for the world to use while Beijing aggressively offers an alternative.

There are already calls for the United States to slow AI development or impose broader restrictions in the name of safety and security. Those arguments deserve serious debate.

AI presents real risks. Advanced semiconductor technology has genuine military applications. Export controls can be an important national-security tool. But every restriction also has consequences.

The question should be whether a restriction actually improves American security without unnecessarily strengthening China's competing technology ecosystem. Because China isn't pausing. Huawei isn't pausing. And global demand for AI computing certainly isn't pausing.

Somebody will provide the chips. Somebody will provide the computing infrastructure. Somebody will provide the software. Somebody will establish the standards.

The United States has a direct strategic interest in American companies remaining central to that ecosystem.

The previous generation of American leaders watched too much manufacturing capacity and too many strategically important supply chains migrate overseas. We should not repeat that mistake with the infrastructure of artificial intelligence.

Semiconductors are no longer merely components inside computers. Compute is strategic power.

The nations and companies controlling advanced computing will possess enormous advantages in scientific discovery, medicine, manufacturing, intelligence, cybersecurity and military technology. That is why the Trump-Xi meeting matters far beyond whatever trade agreement or diplomatic communiqué emerges from Washington.

The two presidents represent countries competing over something much larger: Who builds the technological infrastructure of the 21st century?

The United States should protect its most sensitive technology, its intellectual property and technologies with significant military applications. At the same time, American companies will continue competing for commercial markets around the world.

Design the chips here. Build the semiconductor infrastructure here. Develop the software here. Protect the technology that truly must be protected. And keep American technology innovative and competitive enough that countries around the world continue choosing the American ecosystem instead of Huawei's.

The AI Cold War is already underway. And the chips are the battlefield.

item.title: Trump to meet with Mamdani in New York amid high-stakes midterm push
item.description: Zohran Mamdani will host Donald Trump at Gracie Mansion on Monday for their third face-to-face meeting to discuss issues affecting NYC residents.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will meet with President Donald Trump at Gracie Mansion on Monday to discuss issues affecting New York City and its residents, the mayor's office confirmed to Fox News.

The discussion will take place at Gracie Mansion, the official residence of New York City's mayor. City Hall said it will focus on issues affecting America's largest city.

DSA-BACKED CANDIDATES ARE WINNING PRIMARIES AND THEIR VISION FOR AMERICA IS VERY DIFFERENT

A time for the meeting has not been announced, and the White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for additional details.

Monday's sit-down will mark the third face-to-face meeting between Trump and Mamdani. The two first met in the Oval Office in November 2025, shortly after Mamdani won New York City's mayoral election, and met again at the White House in February.

DSA-BACKED CANDIDATES ARE WINNING PRIMARIES AND THEIR VISION FOR AMERICA IS VERY DIFFERENT

It also comes as New York City prepares to host world leaders for the United Nations General Assembly and the campaign for November's midterm elections enters its final weeks.

Mamdani has become one of the nation's highest-profile progressive mayors as progressive Democrats and Democratic Socialists of America-backed candidates have won several high-profile primaries this election cycle, fueling a broader debate over the Democratic Party's direction ahead of the midterms.

During their first Oval Office meeting in November, Trump and Mamdani said they had discussed housing, affordability and other issues affecting New Yorkers despite their political differences, and both expressed optimism about working together where they could.

Monday's meeting will be their latest opportunity to continue those discussions.

item.title: Scary scene as Jayden Reed carted off on spine board during Packers game against the Jets
item.description: Jayden Reed was carted off on a spine board after a significant blow to the head on a swing pass from Jordan Love during the Packers-Jets game.
item.content:encoded:
There was a scary scene Sunday early in the Green Bay Packers game against the New York Jets when wide receiver Jayden Reed was carted off the field with an apparent neck injury.

Trainers and doctors brought out the cart and put a motionless Reed on a long spine board to protect the player from suffering further damage.

The entire Green Bay Packers team looked on as they watched from both the field and the sideline.

Reed collapsed to the turf when he was hit by Jets linebacker Demario Davis on the second play of the game.

It was a scary scene because no one at the time knew Reed's status as they watched him carted away.

The Packers have ruled Reed out for the remainder of the game with a neck injury. No further updates are currently available as there have been no ensuing press box announcements to the media.

'THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Reed suffered the injury after taking a significant blow to the head on a swing pass from quarterback Jordan Love.

Reed has struggled with injuries before. He missed 10 games last season after breaking his collarbone and then also requiring foot surgery.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

item.title: 1619 Project founder regrets school choice for her daughter, admits putting ideals ahead of her education
item.description: Nikole Hannah-Jones says she regrets her Brooklyn public school choice after her daughter said she never got the education she truly wanted.
item.content:encoded:
New York Times Magazine reporter and creator of the controversial 1619 Project, Nikole Hannah-Jones, acknowledged Sunday that she regretted aspects of the decision to send her daughter to predominantly Black, high-poverty public schools in Brooklyn, New York, after the now-16-year-old told her she did not receive the education she wanted — a decade after Hannah-Jones described the choice as an effort to challenge school segregation.

In a newly released New York Times Magazine essay, Hannah-Jones described revisiting years of emails with her daughter Najya’s teachers and principals and confronting what she called a truth she could no longer suppress.

"Now I felt overcome with regret. Najya deserved better," Hannah-Jones said. "They all did. But she was mine. This girl, my only child, looked to me to protect her, to give her what she needed to thrive. And I had not chosen her."

Hannah-Jones told Fox News Digital on Sunday that the broader focus should remain on families who lack the resources to pursue better educational options for their children.

"I hope people concerned about the choice my husband and I made for our daughter will have equal or more outrage for the thousands of Black children whose parents don’t have the resources to send them to better schools," she said. "As I write in the piece, there is no absolution to be had for any of us."

POWERFUL TEACHERS' UNIONS SHARE STRIKING LINK WITH STATES STRUGGLING TO TEACH KIDS TO READ

Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation and longtime school choice advocate, responded to Hannah-Jones' essay in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing parents should prioritize their children's individual educational needs.

"Parents should put their children first. They should not sacrifice them to a failing government school system in the name of ideology," DeAngelis said. "Nikole Hannah-Jones now says she regrets putting her ideals ahead of her daughter’s education. That admission is long overdue."

"I welcome Nikole Hannah-Jones to the school choice revolution," he continued. "Maybe she will start to understand that pulling her daughter from the failing school system would have done more to improve those schools — through competition — than the status quo ever did. You don’t fix public schools by locking kids in them without any accountability. You fix them by giving them a reason to change their ways."

NEW YORK JOINS FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE INITIATIVE DESPITE TRADITIONAL DEMOCRAT OPPOSITION

Hannah-Jones said the realization culminated in a conversation with Najya as she was writing the essay. She apologized to her daughter after reviewing problems that had followed her through elementary and middle school.

"I feel like you got cheated," Hannah-Jones said. "And I’m sorry for that."

Najya responded by telling her mother that she wished her own education had received greater consideration alongside Hannah-Jones' broader concerns about educational inequality.

"Sometimes I wish instead of always thinking about other kids, you would have thought about me. I never really got the education I wanted," Najya said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’

Hannah-Jones’ assessment marked a shift from the position she described in a widely discussed 2016 New York Times Magazine essay, when she explained why she and her husband enrolled Najya at P.S. 307, a Brooklyn school that was then overwhelmingly Black and Latino and served a largely low-income population. Hannah-Jones said at the time she believed middle-class families could help improve segregated schools by enrolling their children and investing in them.

"I worried — I worry still — about whether I made the right decision for our little girl. But I knew I made the just one," Hannah-Jones said in 2016.

The new essay detailed academic problems that became more apparent as Najya grew older. At Unison, her middle school, Najya earned strong grades and took honors courses, but later said she and her friends realized that they were not being sufficiently challenged. 

Hannah-Jones described limited homework, inexperienced teachers and gaps in her daughter's math preparation that became especially apparent after Najya entered a more academically demanding high school.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Unison Principal Emily Paige acknowledged in the essay that some attempts to accommodate students who entered the school academically behind had unintended consequences, including the decision to eliminate homework.

"It is important to not, in our pursuit of being antiracist, lower expectations," Paige said. "Because this is what happens, right? It’s racism under the guise of antiracism."

DeAngelis told Fox News Digital that Hannah-Jones’ experience should lead her to support policies allowing education funding to follow children to schools selected by their families.

"Hannah-Jones can afford better options. Most families cannot," DeAngelis said. "She should fight for the funding to follow the student so more parents have the same educational opportunities she can buy for herself. School choice is an equalizer."

The debate comes as school choice remains an active issue in New York.

Fox News Digital reported last week that teachers' unions were opposing Democratic New York Gov. Kathy Hochul's plan to participate in a federal tax-credit scholarship program designed to help families pay for educational options outside their assigned schools.

The New York Times' 1619 Project is a long-form collaboration that seeks to "reframe the country's history" by bringing slavery and racism to the forefront of the national narrative. 

While praised by liberals, the project has faced intense scrutiny and pushback from prominent historians who have publicly disputed its factual accuracy, particularly its claims regarding the motivations behind the American Revolution.

Despite the criticism, the 1619 Project's theories of American history were later developed into an educational curriculum with the help of the Pulitzer Center.

Fox News Digital reached out to New York Public Schools for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Kevin Costner sparks romance rumors after grocery run with lifestyle coach
item.description: Kevin Costner was photographed grocery shopping in Santa Barbara with 40-year-old lifestyle coach Jennifer Milburn, sparking new romance rumors.
item.content:encoded:
Kevin Costner sparked romance rumors when he was spotted out shopping recently.

The 71-year-old "Yellowstone" star was photographed shopping at a local Albertsons in Santa Barbara, California, with a woman the Daily Mail identified as 40-year-old lifestyle coach Jennifer Milburn.

The pair were photographed smiling as they walked down the aisles of the grocery store and through the parking lot together, taking turns pushing the shopping cart around.

Costner kept it casual in a pair of white jeans and a white collared shirt, which he paired with flip-flops and black sunglasses.

SCOTT EASTWOOD SAYS HIS FATHER SENT KEVIN COSTNER HOME FROM SET WHILE FILMING 'A PERFECT WORLD'

Milburn opted for a pair of cutoff denim shorts and a long-sleeve white button-up shirt, which she paired with brown sandals and sunglasses. She wore her long blonde hair in a ponytail.

Fox News Digital has reached out to a representative for Costner for comment.

Before stepping out with Milburn, Costner sparked romance rumors with country singer Jewel in December 2023, when photos obtained by TMZ showed her speaking into a microphone and appearing to sit on Costner’s lap, with his arms around her waist.

The "Horizon: An American Saga" star cleared up the rumors during an appearance on "The Howard Stern Show" in June 2024, explaining the photos were taken on Richard Branson's private island, Necker Island, and that he didn't know she was going to be there until he got on the plane.

item.title: DHS chief fires back at Jayapal over claim majority of immigration arrests pose 'no threat'
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin rejected Pramila Jayapal's claim that most ICE arrests over the summer involved individuals who pose "no threat" to public safety, citing angel families.
item.content:encoded:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin pushed back on Rep. Pramila Jayapal’s, D-Wash., claim that the "majority of people" arrested by DHS pose "absolutely no threat to public safety."

Mullin rejected Jayapal’s characterization on "Saturday in America," saying DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) remain committed to targeting high-risk individuals to keep American communities safe and arguing that crimes committed by illegal immigrants have led to tragedy.

"If we're going to have national security in this country, we [need to] know everybody that's entered this country. And so, I'm not going to release you back into the public once we know that you entered this country legally," Mullin said. "It's time for you to go home."

BORDER CZAR TOM HOMAN FIRES BACK AFTER DEMOCRAT CHRIS MURPHY CLAIMS ICE IS ‘TERRORIZING LITTLE KIDS’

"All the angel families that lost their loved ones at the hands of an illegal is 100% preventable, because that illegal shouldn't be in our country to begin with," the DHS boss added.

Jayapal, the ranking member of the House Subcommittee on Immigration, Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and a vocal ICE critic, argued that immigration enforcement under the Trump administration has targeted immigrants without criminal convictions.

"For the first time this summer, the majority of people that DHS arrested were people who pose absolutely no threat to public safety, and the number of people with criminal convictions who are arrested by ICE actually decreased — decreased, not increased," Jayapal said during a hearing last week.

"That’s because when DHS expends all of its energy to go after parents, longtime friends, neighbors, when [Homeland Security Investigations] agents who are supposed to investigate serious crime and human trafficking are instead being moved to street sweeps and riding along with local police for random traffic stops, we are less safe, not more safe," she added.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION

ICE arrested nearly 51,000 illegal immigrants nationwide in August, marking the highest monthly total on record, according to DHS. The department also says ICE has deported more than 2,000 known or suspected terrorists since Trump took office.

"When you have a car accident, and you came… into this country legally, and the Democrats want to say, you're not a criminal and you kill somebody. Yes, you were a criminal and now… you ruined somebody else's life, and now you're a murderer at the same time," the DHS chief said.

"It's political for them. They want to say this every day," he added.

DHS regularly publicizes arrests and deportations involving illegal immigrants convicted of crimes including murder, child pornography, sexual assault and drug trafficking.

"When you decide you're going to break our immigration policies, and you're going to cut the line, you're going to step across our southern border, you're going to step across our northern border. You're still a criminal. We’re still gonna arrest you," the DHS chief said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jayapal’s office for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Nicki Minaj offers career advice to young Americans, delivers blunt response to Trump critics
item.description: Rapper Nicki Minaj revealed her path from Red Lobster to global stardom and fiercely defended her support of President Donald Trump in an exclusive interview.
item.content:encoded:
Rapper Nicki Minaj shared her career advice to young Americans entering the workforce and fiercely defended her support of President Donald Trump during an exclusive interview with "The Ingraham Angle" on Friday.

The music mogul opened up about her journey to the top, explaining how she hustled her way from serving biscuits at Red Lobster to dominating music charts around the world and collaborating with some of the biggest names in Hollywood.

"I did customer service for telephone companies. I was a telemarketer. I sold fire extinguishers. I did everything," Minaj shared with Fox News.

NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

MARY J BLIGE CREDITS FAITH, PASTORS WITH CONFRONTING HER PRIDE AS SHE TOOK CONTROL OF HER CAREER

"What I would tell young people is: This is not the best part of your life, but it is probably one of the most important parts of your life," she said.

Minaj said the lessons she learned, as well as the values she developed while doing "nitty-gritty" work, before money and international success, remain central to how she conducts business today.

"The things that I learned during that time in my life, it still helps me today," the rapper explained. "All the people skills, and the communication skills, and all the problem-solving that I learned then, it still applies now when I'm around superstars or rich people."

"All of those skills, they carry over into the rest of your life. So don't look at that part of your life as something that you can't wait to fly by because… you might not be making the biggest money, but you're doing the real nitty-gritty work that is going to help you for the rest of your life," Minaj added.

THE RICH HAVE ONE FINANCIAL HABIT MOST AMERICANS IGNORE AT THEIR PERIL

The "Super Bass" and "Starships" singer, who has an estimated net worth of $150 million according to Celebrity Net Worth, also advised young Americans to save money, saying that "no matter how little" she made, she would always set aside funds for a rainy day.

Minaj also discussed her support for President Donald Trump after emerging as one of his fiercest allies in Hollywood.

The rapper recently partnered with the Trump administration on the Small Business Administration’s Million Dollar Pitch Competition, serving as one of the celebrity judges.

LIL WAYNE PRAISES TRUMP'S WHITE HOUSE BALLROOM PROJECT, CALLS OUT CRITICS WHO 'DON'T KNOW NOTHING'

The competition brought five small business owners before a panel of judges, including Minaj and Airbnb’s co-founder, to give their best pitch for a share of a $1 million cash prize pool.

"Small business represents the heart of the country…," said Minaj. "You don't have to be a huge household name to be recognized by the president and to be recognized by us."

Minaj, whom Trump has called a "fantastic person," addressed the grief she receives for supporting the president, telling Fox News that she has "absolutely nothing" to say to critics and adding that she is "honored" to work with the administration.

"[Trump] is fun," the rapper said. "He's not just smart and he's not just the president, but he's also someone that I can relate to."

DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’

"He's very grounded. It's easy to connect with him, it's easy feel like he heard you, he understands you," she continued. "And I just love him, and I'm not going to ever make excuses for that."

Minaj was also asked when her fans, whom she fondly refers to as "Barbz," can expect her next tour following a hiatus after her Pink Friday 2 World Tour in 2024. 

She urged fans to give her some time as she embraces what she described as her "businesswoman era."

"Who set you up to asking this question? Is one of the Barbz back there?" she asked host Laura Ingraham. "I'm gonna go out as soon as I present the Barbz with this next body of work, whenever that will be."

"Barbz, I love you very much if you're watching, and I don't want any more questions about concerts. I'm in my businesswoman era," she added.

item.title: Scammers are buying Google ads to steal bank logins
item.description: Federal prosecutors say criminals bought sponsored search ads mimicking real banks, capturing over 5,000 login credentials and draining accounts.
item.content:encoded:
You need to check your bank account, so you open Google, type in your bank's name and click the first result that looks right. Most of us have done some version of that without thinking twice.

Now federal investigators say criminals turned that everyday habit into a way to steal bank logins and drain accounts. The Justice Department announced on Sept. 8 that a Russian web developer accused of helping run a large bank account takeover operation had been extradited to the United States. Prosecutors say the group bought sponsored search engine links that sent banking customers to fake login pages. Victims then entered their credentials, believing they had reached their bank.

That should get the attention of anyone who banks online. Here's how the scam works, why those sponsored results can look so convincing and what you can do to avoid handing your bank login to a criminal.

ASKED SIRI TO CALL YOUR BANK? A SCAM COULD COST THOUSANDS

NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com

According to federal prosecutors, the alleged operation used spoofed domains that mimicked websites belonging to federally insured financial institutions. The conspirators then bought sponsored search engine links. Those links could appear when someone searched for their bank.

A click sent the customer to a fraudulent login page. Once victims entered their credentials, the attackers could capture that information. Prosecutors say the group then used the stolen credentials to access real bank accounts, check balances and initiate unauthorized wire transfers.

The indictment also alleges that Sergei Anatolyevich Filimonov developed and maintained infrastructure supporting the operation. That included databases storing more than 5,000 stolen login credentials and software designed to capture sensitive authentication data.

The newest Sept. 8 Justice Department announcement says the conspirators purchased sponsored search-engine links. It does not name a particular search engine. However, the DOJ previously described the same bank account takeover operation when it seized the group's backend domain in December 2025. In that announcement, investigators specifically said the criminal group delivered fraudulent advertisements through search engines including Google and Bing. The ads imitated sponsored search ads used by legitimate banks.

Victims who clicked those ads were redirected to fake banking websites controlled by the criminals, according to the DOJ. That earlier investigation had identified at least 19 victims across the United States by December 2025. The DOJ reported approximately $28 million in attempted losses and about $14.6 million in actual losses tied to those victims.

Microsoft told CyberGuy that it has policies and detection mechanisms designed to help prevent misleading advertising. The company said that when it becomes aware of ads that violate its policies, it takes action to remove them and uses what it learns to strengthen its detection capabilities. Microsoft also encourages users to report suspicious ads through its "Report a Concern" form. We also reached out to Google for comment but did not hear back before our deadline.

FAKE PATIENT PORTAL SCAM CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN AND INFECT YOUR PC

The trap works because a paid search result can appear in a place many of us naturally look first. You search for your bank. A result appears near the top. The wording looks familiar, so you click before studying the address. Most search ads are legitimate.

Still, the FBI warns that criminals can buy ads that imitate real businesses and direct users to convincing phishing sites. The FBI refers to this tactic as SEO poisoning in its account takeover guidance. That changes how I would approach something as sensitive as online banking. In fact, the FBI specifically recommends using bookmarks or favorites to reach login pages rather than clicking search results or advertisements.

This problem stretches far beyond one alleged criminal operation. Since January 2025, the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center has received more than 5,100 complaints reporting account takeover fraud. Reported losses have exceeded $262 million.

Criminals use several ways to get inside accounts. Fraudulent banking websites remain one of them. The FBI says victims can encounter a phishing site after clicking a fake search advertisement. Attackers may also try to obtain a one-time passcode if an account uses multifactor authentication.

Once criminals gain access, they may move money to accounts they control. That can make recovery difficult, especially when funds move quickly.

The latest development centers on Sergei Anatolyevich Filimonov, 36, a Russian national and web developer. A federal grand jury indicted Filimonov on Nov. 4, 2025. Authorities later extradited him from the Republic of Georgia.

You do not need to stop banking online. However, changing how you reach your bank's login page can lower your risk.

SHOULD YOU USE A SEPARATE COMPUTER FOR ONLINE BANKING?

If you already have your bank's verified app installed, open it directly rather than searching for your bank in a browser. That removes the search-result step where this particular scam tries to catch you.

Visit your bank's verified website and save it as a bookmark or favorite. The FBI specifically recommends bookmarks or favorites for financial login pages instead of relying on search results or advertisements.

Take a second to inspect the domain before you enter banking credentials. A fake site may use a misspelled address or another small change designed to look legitimate. The FBI warns that fraudulent search ads can lead to URLs that closely resemble the real address. Microsoft also advises users to carefully review website URLs before entering credentials or other personal information online.

A "Sponsored" label means someone paid to place the advertisement. So when money or sensitive information is involved, verify the destination yourself before you sign in.

Enable two-factor or multifactor authentication if your financial institution offers it. However, do not let that give you a false sense of security. The FBI warns that MFA may not protect you after you land on a fraudulent login page. Criminals can also use social engineering to try to obtain your one-time code. Never give a one-time passcode to someone who contacts you unexpectedly.

YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES

A trusted password manager can help because it associates your saved login with a particular website. If your password manager normally fills your banking credentials but suddenly does not, stop before typing them manually. Check the address first. We've previously explained how password managers can provide another clue when you land on a spoofed login page.

Strong antivirus software can add another layer of protection if you click a malicious search result. It may warn you about known phishing sites, block dangerous downloads and stop other threats before they reach your device. However, no security software can protect you if you willingly enter your banking credentials on a convincing fake site, so always check the web address first. item.title: See inside the abandoned 95-year-old LA church that just became a luxury hotel
item.description: Hotel Lucile transformed a 1931 Silver Lake church in Los Angeles into a 25-room boutique hotel, preserving stained glass and wood flooring.
item.content:encoded:
A building that has stood in Los Angeles for nearly a century is welcoming visitors in an entirely new way after an extensive restoration.

The former Bethany Presbyterian Church, built in 1931 in the city's Silver Lake neighborhood, has been converted into Hotel Lucile, a 25-room boutique hotel with a courtyard cocktail pool that opened Sept. 14, according to a hotel news release shared with Fox News Digital.

The property has taken on several roles over the decades. After operating as a church, it was later used as a theater and an antique market before being converted into a hotel, according to the release.

RENTALS NOW ALLOWED IN HISTORIC WATER TOWER ON KING CHARLES' SANDRINGHAM ESTATE WHERE ROYALS SPEND CHRISTMAS

The latest transformation was about seven and a half years in the making, Anthony Gutierrez, opening general manager of Hotel Lucile, told Fox News Digital.

The restoration focused on finding a new use for the building while maintaining elements that date to its time as a house of worship, Gutierrez said.

Many of the church's original features remain throughout the property, including stained-glass windows, wooden beams, high ceilings and steel-framed windows.

One of the biggest transformations took place inside the former chapel, which now serves as the hotel's restaurant and dining room.

"Literally just about every aspect of the chapel itself was preserved," Gutierrez said, pointing to the original wood flooring, beams and stained-glass windows.

Preserving those features while preparing the building for its new use required extensive work, Gutierrez said. Crews removed the chapel's original wood flooring to install modern electrical and plumbing systems and add soundproofing for the guest rooms before putting the flooring back into place.

"For the dining room itself, it is as original as it can be," he said, estimating that about 90% of the space remains original.

Working with a building approaching 100 years old also presented challenges throughout the years-long redevelopment.

"We had surprises up until the day when we received our certificate of occupancy," Gutierrez said. "It was not an easy journey."

Meeting modern requirements while trying to preserve the building's original architectural elements made parts of the restoration a "painstaking" process, he added.

The building's latest chapter also includes an art collection, with two large hand-painted murals in the former chapel and other works displayed throughout the property.

Some pieces are part of a permanent collection, while others are available for purchase, Gutierrez said.

Along with preserving elements of the former church, the property has introduced modern touches, including an Erewhon-curated minibar and a roving martini cart that makes its rounds each evening, according to the release.

Gutierrez said the combination of old and new can offer travelers something different from a traditional hotel experience.

"There is some comfort in things being the same, but taking even a small risk of just going somewhere different and experiencing something different can really bring kind of a highlight to a trip or even a staycation," he said.

item.title: Ernie Accorsi, legendary Giants general manager who made the shrewd move to get Eli Manning, dead at 84
item.description: Ernie Accorsi, the Giants GM who executed the blockbuster 2004 NFL Draft trade for Eli Manning, has died at 84. Eli Manning shared an emotional tribute.
item.content:encoded:
Ernie Accorsi, a legendary New York Giants front office executive who helped build the roster that made it to Super Bowl XXXV and traded for Eli Manning, has died, the team said. He was 84.

Accorsi was the Giants’ general manager from 1998 to 2006. He was also the general manager of the Baltimore Colts and the executive vice president of football operations for the Cleveland Browns.

"It was the honor of my dad’s lifetime to represent the Baltimore Colts, Cleveland Browns, and New York Giants, three organizations that meant so much to him throughout his remarkable career," the Accorsi family said. "Our family is deeply grateful to each of them and to the many people who became lifelong friends along the way.

"We are especially grateful to the New York Giants organization, John Mara, Ronnie Barnes, and the late Wellington Mara for their friendship, loyalty, and love for my father over so many years. The Giants were far more than a team to him. They were family, and being part of that family was something he treasured. Once a Giant, always a Giant."

The Giants released a statement on Accorsi’s death hours before the start of the majority of the NFL’s Week 2 slate.

"Ernie helped shape the course of New York Giants history through his vision, leadership and unwavering belief in building a championship organization," Giants president John Mara said in a statement. "Beyond his accomplishments as a football executive, he was a trusted advisor and dear friend. His legacy will forever be part of the Giants, and he will be greatly missed."

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell also reflected on Accorsi’s life and impact.

"Ernie Accorsi was one of the most respected football minds in NFL history and a dear friend whose wisdom and perspective I valued tremendously," he said. "Throughout his remarkable career, he shaped championship-caliber clubs and earned the admiration of everyone who worked with him.

"Ernie's impact extended beyond the teams he served. As co-chair of the General Managers Advisory Committee, he helped guide our game and strengthen the NFL. His integrity, common sense and commitment to doing what was best for football made him an invaluable voice. Ernie was thoughtful, humble, and he cared deeply about the people in our league. He never lost sight of the relationships that make football special and we will all greatly miss him."

Accorsi executed the trade that brought Manning to the Giants during the 2004 NFL Draft. The team traded the rights to Philip Rivers to the San Diego Chargers for the former Ole Miss standout.

The move changed the history of the Giants as Manning would eventually guide the team to two Super Bowl titles during his career.

"I was extremely sad to hear the news about Ernie," Manning said in a statement. "I call Ernie every draft week for the last 12 years, maybe longer than that, and just thank him for making the trade and believing in me and bringing me to the New York Giants. I know he was the believer in me and kind of the reason I got here.

"I appreciated him so much for building such great teams and giving us the opportunity to win some championships here. He was always so fun to sit with and just talk, whether it’s the Giants or his time in Baltimore around the Colts. His stories around the NFL and the people he was around that shaped his career were always so entertaining. I know the Giants organization owes a lot of thanks to Ernie Accorsi and what he was able to do for the organization."

The Giants inducted Accorsi into their Ring of Honor in 2016 with Tom Coughlin and Justin Tuck.

item.title: Why Trump zeroed in on Greenland, the world’s largest island, mostly covered in ice — in 3 charts
item.description: President Donald Trump says his Greenland deal gives the U.S. permanent control over the island's security while barring China and Russia from Arctic footholds.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump’s Greenland push has moved from threats to a new security agreement with Denmark and Greenland that he says will give the United States "permanent control" over the island’s security and allow Washington to expand its military presence there.

The agreement still requires approval from Danish and Greenlandic lawmakers. Its full terms have not been made public, but officials say it would leave Greenland under Danish sovereignty while barring China, Russia and other non-NATO adversaries from establishing military bases or making certain sensitive investments on the island.

TRUMP THREATENS TARIFFS ON COUNTRIES OPPOSING GREENLAND TAKEOVER PLANS

Greenland rarely draws global attention. But as Arctic ice melts and great powers compete for influence, the world’s largest island has become a strategic prize. A semi-autonomous territory of Denmark, Greenland is home to a key U.S. military base and sits near emerging shipping routes and critical mineral deposits.

Greenland’s roughly 56,000 residents are spread across five municipalities, with most living in small coastal towns. About 80% of the island is covered by an ice sheet, leaving much of its vast interior uninhabited. Despite its small population, Greenland is nearly the size of Alaska and Texas combined.

Its location off Canada’s northeastern coast places Greenland at the heart of Arctic defense planning. The U.S. has maintained a military outpost in northwestern Greenland since 1953 at Pituffik Space Base, now operated by the U.S. Space Force. Russia also maintains military installations in the region, while China has sought greater access since declaring itself a "near-Arctic state" in 2018.

Retreating Arctic ice is opening shipping lanes around the island that could shorten trade routes between North America, Europe and Asia.

The changing landscape has also drawn attention to Greenland’s rare earth elements and other critical minerals used in technology, renewable energy and military systems.

CHINA’S GRIP ON RARE-EARTH MAGNETS COULD CRUSH US DRONE INDUSTRY BEFORE IT GROWS

Rare earth elements are especially important in high-performance magnets used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, generators and precision-guidance systems. They are also used in missile guidance, radar, sonar, satellites and advanced aircraft.

China dominates the global rare-earth supply chain, accounting for roughly 60% of mining and more than 90% of processing capacity. As the U.S. and European Union seek to reduce their reliance on Beijing, Greenland has emerged as a potential counterweight.

Trump’s agreement may fall short of his earlier goal of bringing Greenland under U.S. control, but it could still give Washington a larger military and strategic foothold in the Arctic.

As competition over shipping routes, defense positioning and critical minerals intensifies, Greenland’s importance is likely to grow.

item.title: Christine Taylor’s ‘Hey Dude’ salary was far lower than castmates remembered
item.description: Christine Taylor says her "Hey Dude" salary was just $3,500 per episode, far less than her castmates remembered earning on the Nickelodeon series.
item.content:encoded:
Christine Taylor is looking back at her early Hollywood career — and revealing that her "Hey Dude" salary was far lower than her castmates remembered.

During an appearance on "The Secret World of Alex Mack" actress Natanya Ross’ "We’re Still Here, Babe" podcast Wednesday, Taylor — who played Melody Hanson on Nickelodeon’s Western comedy series from 1989 to 1991 — said she earned approximately $3,500 per episode by the show’s final season.

"By the time ‘Hey Dude’ ended, we had this discussion among our castmates, and everyone seemed to think [that] by the last season, we were making $5,000 an episode," Taylor said.

"No, we were making $3,500 an episode, I’m pretty sure, because they would bump us up $500 every season," she added.

Taylor said all of the cast members earned the same amount, despite her co-stars’ shared belief that they were making $5,000 per episode.

"Everyone in their brain was like, ‘$5,000.’ I was like, ‘No way, no way. That would have… no, it did not happen,’" she recalled.

The actress said she was careful with the money she earned while working on the popular children’s series. She also credited her family with helping her financially as she moved to Los Angeles and pursued acting.

JENNIE GARTH ADMITS ‘SCARY’ FINANCIAL SPIRAL AFTER ‘90210’ FAME

Taylor remembered budgeting closely, using laundromats and monitoring her spending during the early stages of her career.

The actress went on to appear in "Saved by the Bell," "Blossom" and "Robin Hood: Men in Tights" before landing her breakout role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie."

‘BRADY BUNCH’ STAR SHARES THE SIMPLE WORD THAT SAVED HER FROM HOLLYWOOD TRAPS

Taylor also revealed that she was asked to lose 10 pounds before playing the iconic character in the 1995 film.

"Of course, I was embarrassed when that ask came my way," she said, adding that the request reflected the attitudes of the 1990s and "would never happen today."

FORMER DISNEY STAR DYLAN SPROUSE SAYS ACTING AS A KID WAS ‘CHILD LABOR’

Taylor later starred alongside her husband, Ben Stiller, in films, including "Zoolander" and "DodgeBall." The couple married in 2000, separated in 2017 and later reconciled. They share two children, Ella and Quinlin.

Taylor’s experience is part of a broader pattern in Hollywood, where a recognizable television role does not always guarantee financial security. Several former television stars have revealed that their salaries and residual checks were dramatically different from what audiences assumed.

JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS

"The Sopranos" star Drea de Matteo recently said she was forced to find alternative income after acting work slowed down. The actress revealed that she turned to OnlyFans after facing financial difficulties and a lien on her home.

During an appearance on Jamie Kennedy’s podcast, de Matteo said she earned enough through the platform to pay off a $75,000 lien within 75 minutes of posting a bikini photo. She also said she sometimes earned approximately $100,000 per month.

More recently, "Married... with Children" star Ted McGinley revealed that he receives extremely small residual checks from some of his popular television projects, despite starring in long-running shows.

item.title: Obama criticizes Trump on approach to AI, escalates warning for stronger regulation
item.description: Barack Obama slammed Trump's AI stance at Colgate University, warning the administration is neither capable nor willing to build a regulatory framework.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Barack Obama criticized President Donald Trump's approach to artificial intelligence on Friday, calling for stronger federal regulation as the technology rapidly advances and concerns grow over safety, jobs and human control.

"The challenge we have is that, obviously, we have a president currently that has said that’s for losers," Obama said during an appearance at Colgate University in Hamilton, New York. "So we’ve got a gap of at least a couple of years, where things are moving really fast, and we have an administration that is not capable of or willing to — I would argue both — putting together a serious regulatory framework."

Obama's remarks expanded on a warning he issued last week, when he privately urged Democrats to make AI a central political issue. 

DEMOCRATS EMBRACED AI’S GROWTH BEFORE TRUMP CAME ALONG — NOW THEY WANT TO SLOW IT DOWN

RNC member and Humans First Chairwoman Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital last week that policymakers should recognize AI’s risks without handing greater control to Washington or the technology companies themselves.

"You don't have to agree on politics to recognize reality: AI is moving incredibly fast, and policymakers need to understand both the opportunities and the very real risks that come with it," she said. 

"Where I likely disagree with President Obama is on what government should do about it. The answer isn't handing Washington bureaucrats more control, and it certainly isn't allowing Big Tech to write the rules that govern itself," she said.

"We need guardrails that protect Americans while allowing American innovation to lead the world. That means protecting children, workers and our national security, while making sure China doesn't win the AI race," she continued.

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

The debate shifted again Saturday when Trump announced the creation of an "AI Force" and said he plans to appoint an AI czar, while reiterating that his administration would resist efforts to slow development as the United States competes with China.

"We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry," Trump said in a lengthy Truth Social post.

Obama, speaking during Colgate’s Family Weekend, argued that relying on companies’ financial incentives and potential liability was insufficient to manage the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems.

"[The] government has to be regulating this!" Obama said. "I heard one of Donald Trump’s main advisors on this make the argument that, ‘The market will take care of it. These companies will solve the safety issues because they have every incentive to do so — if it turns out to be dangerous, people will just sue them, and they’re worried about financial liability.’ That’s not how we treat airlines! Or drug companies, or food companies."

Kremer told Fox News Digital that she felt Obama was "directing his criticism at the wrong branch of government."

"It is not the president's job to write laws. That responsibility belongs to Congress, and Congress needs to act," Kremer said.

"We need serious guardrails for artificial intelligence, but this should not become another partisan fight over Donald Trump or Barack Obama. AI is moving too quickly and the stakes are too high for that. Congress must do its job and establish clear, enforceable rules that protect our children, American workers, our national security, and our communities while allowing American innovation to continue," she added.

Kremer also said that Republicans should lead the framework for AI.

"Republicans should also recognize that if we fail to lead on this issue, we leave a political opening for the left to define the debate and write the rules. Conservatives should be leading with a framework that protects Americans, preserves innovation, respects states' rights and local control, and holds Big Tech accountable. We should not cede this issue to Democrats simply because some people believe any guardrail is anti-innovation," she said.

TRUMP’S DATA CENTER PUSH FRACTURES CONGRESS AS LOCAL ANGER EXPLODES: 'GRASPING AT STRAWS'

"Voluntary commitments from the AI companies themselves are not sufficient. The companies developing the most powerful technology in the world cannot also be the only ones deciding whether that technology is safe," Kremer said.

Obama's characterization of the administration came as the White House has pursued its own AI policy framework, though one focused heavily on encouraging development and limiting regulations it considers burdensome.

The Trump administration unveiled a national legislative framework in March addressing child safety, free speech, workforce issues and energy costs while calling for a consistent national approach to AI policy.

Trump also signed a national security directive in June ordering agencies to accelerate adoption of advanced AI while requiring systems used in national security settings to be "robust, steerable, controllable" and subject to clear lines of accountability.

The disagreement has intensified as executives inside the AI industry themselves call for additional safeguards. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged companies last week to slow the pace of improvements to frontier models, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk expressed support for greater caution.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment, but did not immediately hear back.

item.title: California animal rescue operator charged with felonies for alleged 'inhumane and unsanitary conditions'
item.description: Video shows the squalid conditions where 300 animals were found at Christine De Anda's unlicensed Los Angeles County kennel, leading to 35 charges.
item.content:encoded:
A California animal rescue operator is facing up to 24 1/2 years in state prison after being charged with 35 felonies and misdemeanors for alleged cruelty to animals, as she is accused of leaving roughly 300 animals living in severe squalor.

Christine De Anda, 57, operator of the "Rock ‘N’ Pawz" rescue, faces 12 felony counts of animal cruelty, two felony counts of grand theft of labor, and 21 misdemeanor charges ranging from failure to provide care to operating an unlicensed kennel, according to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office.

Prosecutors requested that her bail be set at $914,500 ahead of her arraignment at the Antelope Valley Courthouse.

FLORIDA MAIL CARRIER ACCUSED OF SNATCHING PETS ON ROUTE, TRAPPING 100-PLUS CATS AND DOGS IN ‘HOARDING’ HOUSE

"For someone who calls herself an animal rescuer, there’s a fundamental responsibility to protect and care for the animals entrusted to her," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman said. "Instead, purported rescuer Christine De Anda allegedly left these animals to suffer or die from starvation, dehydration, untreated injuries and painful urine and fecal burns in filthy conditions."

"After repeated citations and warnings, Ms. De Anda continued taking in animals she could not care for, leaving hundreds to endure prolonged suffering," Hochman added. "These animal victims cannot speak for themselves and look to us to protect them. My office will hold their victimizer fully accountable for her inhumane actions."

The charges stem from a March 20, 2026, search warrant executed by Los Angeles County Animal Care and Control (DACC). Investigators removed more than 300 animals — primarily dogs, but also cats, a pig, a rabbit, a goose and two goats — in what DACC Director Marcia Mayeda called the "largest companion animal search warrant and rescue operation ever conducted" in the department’s history.

117 DEAD DOGS FOUND AT ANIMAL RESCUE, MANY WITH GUNSHOT WOUNDS AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE FOR ANSWERS

"More than 300 animals were removed from severely inhumane conditions," Mayeda said. "Animals were living in and saturated with their own excrement, had serious untreated illnesses and injuries, were emaciated, and were forced to live in small crates without adequate room to properly lie comfortably. Our teams have worked tirelessly to stabilize them, provide the medical care they needed, and help them recover."

At least one cat was found dead from starvation and dehydration at the start of the investigation, authorities said.

FLORIDA MAN ALLEGEDLY KILLS FAMILY'S KITTENS IN FRONT OF TEENAGE DAUGHTER AS FORM OF PUNISHMENT: OFFICIALS

"Sadly, despite all efforts, we were unable to save every animal due to the extent of their illnesses and injuries," Mayeda added. "DACC is deeply grateful for the support of the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Los Angeles, Pasadena Humane and Kern County Animal Services for assisting us with this rescue and the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office for its commitment to pursuing justice for these animals."

The L.A. County DA's Office shared a video on YouTube of the animals at the shelter, showing the conditions that led to the charges.

Prosecutors say De Anda continued to take in an increasing number of animals despite years of citations and warnings regarding her inability to care for them. She is accused of violating multiple county codes, including operating an animal kennel without required land-use approval, maintaining unsanitary conditions and having structures with unpermitted construction, plumbing, electrical and grading work.

item.title: Trump says new arch will also deploy drones, position snipers and store ammo
item.description: Trump says his 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington Memorial Bridge will house drones, snipers and large quantities of ammunition storage.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that his planned triumphal arch near the Arlington Memorial Bridge will be converted into a military complex capable of housing drones, deploying snipers and storing ammunition.

"At the strong request of the United States Military, and for National Security purposes, I have agreed to convert the magnificent Triumphal Arch … into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

TRUMP REVEALS ARC DE TRIOMPHE-STYLE MONUMENT FOR AMERICA’S 250TH ANNIVERSARY

Trump said the 250-foot structure would have the "rapid ability" to deploy large numbers of drones, as well as snipers positioned on the roof and plaza areas. He also said the complex would store "large quantities of sniper ammunition."

"There will be no facility like this anywhere in the World," Trump wrote.

The monument, inspired by Paris’ Arc de Triomphe, is intended to welcome visitors crossing the Memorial Bridge from Arlington National Cemetery into the nation’s capital. The proposed structure would be clad in granite and topped with three golden statues.

FROM THE GILDED OVAL OFFICE TO A NEW BALLROOM: A LOOK AT TRUMP'S WHITE HOUSE PROJECTS

The project has drawn criticism from preservationists, lawmakers and veterans, who argue that it could disrupt views of the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. Opponents have also questioned whether the project requires congressional approval under federal law.

The National Capital Planning Commission has approved the site and preliminary plans, but the project still requires additional review. Construction was previously expected to begin this month.

The arch is one of several major construction and renovation projects Trump has pursued in Washington.

TRUMP GAVE THE OVAL OFFICE A GILDED MAKEOVER – AND COVERED THE COST HIMSELF

The administration has also begun work on a 90,000-square-foot White House ballroom. The sprawling addition, announced last July, will accommodate approximately 650 seated guests and follow the White House’s classical design.

The White House currently lacks a formal ballroom, and the new structure is expected to replace the East Wing. Then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the ballroom was estimated to cost $200 million and would be financed by Trump and private donors.

The ballroom is not the only update.

Trump has introduced gold accents in the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, lined the "walk of fame" with portraits of former presidents, including a photo of the autopen representing former President Joe Biden’s time in office, added stone pavers to the Rose Garden lawn and installed two 88-foot flagpoles.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for additional comment.

item.title: Waltz delivers blunt warning to nations defying Iran sanctions, touts Greenland deal
item.description: Ambassador Mike Waltz says President Trump will push Gulf leaders and allies to enforce Iran sanctions at the United Nations, warning of consequences for noncompliance.
item.content:encoded:
UNITED NATIONS, NEW YORK: President Donald Trump will return to the United Nations this week seeking greater international cooperation in confronting Iran, even as his administration moves to reshape the global institution hosting world leaders, U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview ahead of the gathering.

With the U.S.-Iran war entering its seventh month, Trump is expected to address the General Assembly on Tuesday and meet Gulf leaders whose countries have been directly affected by the conflict.

The gathering comes as Washington seeks to intensify economic pressure on Tehran, European allies confront Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine, and the administration faces questions about whether its push to reduce the U.N.'s size and spending risks diminishing the organization's ability to respond to international crises.

BESSENT WARNS IRAN'S OUTSIDE BACKERS TO 'STAY AWAY' AS TRUMP SEEKS TO 'ASPHYXIATE' TEHRAN'S ECONOMY

Waltz outlined what Washington expects from its partners on Iran: full enforcement of sanctions against Tehran, with consequences for countries that fail to comply.

"They will reinforce that message, but importantly, it's all of these countries actually enforcing the sanctions and what they're going to hear is there will be consequences for friend and foe," Waltz said. "The president is doing this for the future security of the world."

European and Asian allies have largely resisted Trump's requests for assistance in the Iran conflict, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes in February, Reuters reported on Sept. 18. The war has also disrupted energy markets, with Iran obstructing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and its Houthi allies tightening their grip on a critical Red Sea shipping corridor.

Waltz said the administration intends to make sanctions enforcement a central part of its diplomatic push during UNGA.

"The Iranian economy continues to crater," Waltz said, pointing to the country's currency, inflation and the U.S. naval blockade. "One way or another, the president has been crystal clear on our goals here that Iran cannot and will not have a nuclear weapon."

His remarks follow a Sept. 17 U.N. Security Council vote in which Russia and China blocked an effort to continue independent monitoring of international sanctions on Iran.

Trump is also expected to meet Gulf leaders to discuss the conflict and regional security. Waltz said the administration wants to hear directly from its Gulf partners about their concerns, describing the collective meeting as an important diplomatic opportunity.

JEFF BARTOS SAYS UN REFORM IS NO LONGER AN 'OXYMORON' AFTER $570M IN CUTS

The Iran conflict is unfolding against a broader debate over the future of the United Nations, an institution Trump has repeatedly criticized and his administration has sought to substantially reform.

On Sept. 16, the United States paid $725 million toward the U.N.'s regular budget and another $102 million for peacekeeping operations. The payments reduced Washington's outstanding debt and averted the immediate risk of losing its General Assembly voting rights in 2027. However, the U.S. still owed approximately $1.312 billion to the organization's regular budget, according to the U.N.

Asked why American taxpayers should continue funding an organization the administration has repeatedly criticized for what it considers anti-American bias, Waltz pointed to efforts to reduce spending and redirect the institution toward its original mission.

"The president is clear about getting the U.N. back to basics and helping it realize its potential," Waltz told Fox News Digital.

He said the administration had secured more than $1 billion in budget reductions, with roughly 3,000 headquarters positions being cut and a reduction of approximately 25% in peacekeeping personnel.

"We have the U.N. on a diet," Waltz said.

But Waltz also made clear that the administration does not intend to abandon the United Nations.

"There's got to be one place in the world where everyone can come together and put diplomacy first and can actually talk," he said. "We don't ever want to see a U.N. in Beijing or Moscow or Brussels."

"If we just walked away, you'd have 192 countries talking without us," Waltz added.

Gaza offers one example of how the administration intends to use the U.N. while limiting direct American military involvement. Waltz pointed to the U.N.-endorsed Board of Peace and the planned International Stabilization Force, which is intended to support security and a postwar transition in Gaza. The ambassador said he does not want American troops deployed there, arguing that international security operations should allow other countries to share the burden. The U.N. Security Council endorsed the Gaza peace plan and authorized the stabilization force in November 2025.

The State Department said Sept. 18 that Secretary of State Marco Rubio will be in New York from Sept. 20–23 to meet foreign counterparts, advance U.S. security and economic priorities and continue the administration's campaign for U.N. reform.

WALTZ CALLS OUT IRANIAN DIPLOMAT AT UN FOLLOWING DRONE STRIKES ON BAHRAIN AND KUWAIT

Trump arrives in New York days after announcing a new security agreement with Denmark and Greenland aimed at expanding the American military presence in the Arctic while restricting adversaries from establishing bases or making sensitive investments on the island.

The agreement falls short of Trump's earlier ambition to acquire Greenland, which remains an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark. Denmark and Greenland have stressed that the arrangement will not compromise the island's sovereignty or right to self-determination. Additional details of the agreement have yet to be made public.

Waltz told Fox News Digital that the deal reflects the Arctic's growing strategic importance as melting ice opens new shipping routes and increases access to energy and mineral resources.

"It's incredibly significant," Waltz said, pointing to Russia's Arctic military capabilities and the potential for new shipping routes to transform global trade.

"It took some tough tweets, maybe some tough language," he said. "We now have an agreement with our ally Denmark."

The agreement comes as European governments confront overlapping security challenges involving Russia's war in Ukraine, Arctic defense and uncertainty over transatlantic security arrangements, while Washington seeks greater allied cooperation in its campaign against Iran.

TRUMP ARRIVES AT NATO SUMMIT AS IRAN RIFT LOOMS ABOVE ALLIANCE TALKS

The U.N. expects 73 heads of state and 45 heads of government, along with 49 ministers, 11 vice presidents and one crown prince, to attend High-Level Week, U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric told reporters Friday.

Member states have submitted approximately 1,000 requests for bilateral meetings, while about 168 events are scheduled alongside the official proceedings.

The 81st General Assembly's General Debate begins Tuesday and runs through Sept. 28.

Beyond Iran, world leaders are expected to address Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the future of Gaza, international security and the U.N.'s ability to respond to emerging global challenges.

Waltz described the administration's approach with a slogan inspired by the president's political branding: "Make the U.N. great again."

But the immediate diplomatic questions facing Washington are more concrete: whether allies will increase pressure on Iran, whether Gulf leaders can agree on a path toward ending the conflict and whether the administration's push for a leaner U.N. can coexist with its efforts to use the organization to address international security challenges.

item.title: Electric Mercedes motorhome targets 621-mile range
item.description: The Mercedes-Benz eActros 600 electric truck targets 621 miles per charge on a 28,000-mile round-the-world journey through over 30 countries.
item.content:encoded:
If you think you've seen some wild RVs, this one may reset the scale. Professional truck driver and content creator Tobias Wagner, better known online as Elektrotrucker, is preparing to drive around the world in a specially converted Mercedes-Benz eActros 600. A full Bliss Mobil living module sits behind the cab, turning this electric truck into a rolling home. Wagner plans to make the entire journey on battery power.

Mercedes-Benz Trucks says the route will cover about 28,000 miles through more than 30 countries over roughly one year, with a goal of no more than 80 charging stops. According to Mercedes, the trip would be the first known circumnavigation of the globe in a fully battery-electric truck. What really caught my attention is how far Wagner hopes to go between those stops. Here's how this massive electric motorhome works and why its 621-mile range target could be the toughest part of the trip.

100 KODIAK DRIVERLESS TRUCKS ARE HEADED FOR PUBLIC ROADS
